Moazzem Hossain and six others ------ Petitioners

full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: Writ Petition No. 3006/1998, Writ Petition No. 3007 of 1998, Writ Petition No. 3008 of 1998, Writ Petition No. 3109 of 1998, Writ Petition No. 3421 of 1998, Writ Petition No. 3388 of 1998 and Writ Petition No. 3724 of 1998 and contempt case No. 3 of 1998 were heard one after another, Petitioner of each of the above Rules earlier filed Writ Petition No. 2297 of 1995, 2173 of 1995, 2298 of 1995, 2222 of 1995, 2185 of 1995, 2186 of 1995 and 2451 of 1995 respectively challenging notice under section 17 of the Bank Companies Act 1991 issued on different dates on the petitioner of each of the above Rules and after hearing by a common judgment dated 1-7-97 all those Rules along with other Rules were discharged and said judgment of the High Court Division was upheld by the Appellate Division by judgment dated 29-4-1998 in Civil Petition No. 123 of 1998 and other petitions. 

 5. Petitioner Abu Taher Mia of Writ Petition No. 3109 of 1998 has challenged a similar notice of the same date on the ground of his being absolved of the liabilities by the respondent No. 1 pursuant to a settlement with respondent No. 3, National Bank Ltd during pendency of the Rule in Writ Petition 2451 of 1995 and Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 259 of 1997 by memo dated 6-10-97 (Annexure-D) of the respondent No. 1, Bangladesh Bank and that petitioner was served with a notice under section 17 of the said Act on 25-9-95 as guarantor of Selina Trading Corporation to the extent of Taka 2 lac and that his reply was not found satisfactory by the respondent No. 1 and, as such, he filed Writ Petition No. 2451 of 1995 and that after discharge of the said Rule on 1-7-97 petitioner filed Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 259 of 1997 which was dismissed on 29-4-95 and that while the operation of the said notice was kept in abeyance respondent No. 3 on receipt of the amount of the guarantee decided to absolve the petitioner of his abilities and respondent No. 1 gave approval of the same on 6-10-97 and that thereafter respondent No. 3 by letter dated 7-10-97 (Annexure-F) informed the petitioner about the same and, as such, impugned notice dated 17-9-98 is wholly illegal. 

 12. Similarly, petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3008 of 1998 by filing an affidavit in reply reiterated his earlier statements and also stated that his bank guarantee in favour of Niaz Md Khan was returned by respondent No. 3 by letter dated 7-10-97 (Annexure-X) in favour of Alamgir Sarker was returned by letter dated 2-11-97 (Annexure-X(1) and in favour of Baharuddin Khelon by letter dated 2-11-97 (Annexure X(2) and in favour of Captain Ashraful Islam by letter dated 24-2-97 (Annexure-X(3) and the returned of bank guarantee in favour of Captain Ashraful Islam was approved by the respondent No. 1 on certain condition by letter dated 5-4-97 (Annexure-X(4) and after such absolving of the petitioner from those liabilities he did not proceed with Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 25 of 1997 filed by him and on his prayer Appellate Division dismissed the same on 13-8-97 and that on 10-8-97 respondent No.1 accorded its approval to withdraw the notice under section 17 of the said Act and, as such, petitioner''s vacating the office of director did not arise. 

 13. Petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3421 of 1998 by filing a supplementary affidavit on 8-3-99 stated that respondent No. 4 by letter dated 21-4-97 (Annexure-N) and letter dated 11-5-97 (Annexure-O) approved the proposal of rescheduling the loan of Yunusco Fabric Ltd and requested respondent No.1 to reconsider the proposal for rescheduling and further stated that 12 post-dated cheques (Annexure-P series) were submitted by the petitioner and that the value of the mortgaged property and hypothecated machineries as per expert opinion (Annexure-0 and 01) was. Taka 7,67,38,400.00 and that the petitioner paid 10% of the outstanding loan through deposit slips dated 23-12-96 (Annexure-B) and dated 26-12-96 (Annexure-B(1) and Agrabad Branch of respondent No. 4 by letter dated 24-2-98 (Annexure-B2) acknowledged receipt of the said cheese amounting to Taka 73,48,156.00 and that respondent No. 4 also issued certificate dated 26-10-97 (Annexure-B) stating that the loan of the said company was rescheduled with approval of the respondent No. 1 and Agrabad Branch of respondent No. 4 also issued a similar certificate on 5-10-95 (Annexure-T) stating that the said company deposited instalments upto June 1998 and further stating that respondent No. 1 should have withdrawn the notice under section 17 of the said Act against the petitioner as loan in case of Abdul Awal Mintoo by letter dated 10-8-97 (Annexure-II). Respondent Nos. 3 and 4 by filing another affidavit-in-opposition against the aforesaid supplementary affidavit stated that respondent No. 1 by letter dated 15-4-97 (Annexure-Y) approved rescheduling of the said loan to be paid within 5 years in 60 equal monthly instalments within 31-3-2002 but declined to remit interest; that statements made in the supplementary affidavit are not wholly correct and that Agrabad Branch, respondent No. 4 by it letter dated 13-8-98 (Annexure-Y) (2) informed respondent No. 4 that cheques could not be encashed and it realised instalments upto May 1998 and that the expert valuation of the properties of the said Company was inflated and that instalments for June, July and August, 1998 have not been paid and the sum of Taka 97,74,468.00 as on 8-3-99 had fallen due and no further installment have been paid as per telex dated 9-3-98 (Annexure-Y 3) and that after dismissal of petitioner''s leave petition on 29-4-98 legal consequence of vacating his directorship had flowed and he cannot be appointed director unless he fully repaid the liabilities and expiry of one year from the date of such repayment and that respondent No. 1 by its letter dated 3-6-97 approved renewal of back to back LC limit upto Taka 6 crore and approved packing credit limit of Taka 30 lac as against approval of respondent No. 4 by resolution dated 29-9-96 (Annexure-Y) and that the petitioner did not repay the instalment dues which would be seen from letter dated 26-11-98 (Annexure-Y 5, dated 13-1-98 (Annexure-Y 6) dated 16-5-98 (Annexure-Y 7) dated 22-8-98 (Annexure-Y 8) and dated 10-12-98 (Annexure-Y 9). 

 17. Relying on the observations in the case of Director, National Bank vs Bangladesh Bank, reported in 2 BLC 520 it has been contended by the learned Advocate of the petitioner of the respective Rule that since the over due loan in question was rescheduled or paid or guarantee fulfilled absolving the guarantor from the liability under the guarantee bond during pendency of earlier Writ Petitions, Civil petitions for leave to appeal or Civil Miscellaneous Petition notice under section 17 of the Bank Companies Act 1991 stood cancelled or withdrawn and, as such subsequent impugned notices declaring the office of director of the petitioner of each of the Rules vacant is without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 2. Any person on receipt of a notice under sub-section (I) may within thirty days from the date of receipt of notice send his representation in writing to the Bangladesh Bank, if he has anything to say and also send a copy of the same to the Bank company or Financial Institution, as the case may be, which issued such notice. 

 22. It is pertinent to note that unless any provision of law is struck down by this Court on the ground of violation of fundamental rights or any other provision of the Constitution the court is required to follow the same. However in applying any statutory provision of law in the facts and circumstances of a case before it, this country, by interpretation may restrict or extend the meaning of such provision in the interest of justice to give relief to an aggrieved party. But it cannot give any decision contrary to the relevant statutory provision of law applicable in the case. Even if any decision is made by this Court contrary to any statutory provision of law applicable in the case without noticing the same that decision though binding between the parties is not law declared by this court. Moreover, any observation made by this court in deciding a case contrary to any statutory provision of laws overlooking or oblivious of the same is neither binding on this court nor on any Court subordinate to this court, for statutory provision can only be struck down on the above ground or interpreted in the above manner. So, we are unable to follow the observations made by this Court in the aforesaid decision perincuriam so far as it relates to rescheduling of loan or discharge from the liability of the bank guarantee or payment of the entire dues though one of us was a party to the same in respect of the petitioner of each of the Rules. Their cases in our views should be decided on the basis of amended provisions of section 17 of the said Act rather, than on the basis of observations made in the aforesaid decision overlooking the amended provision. 

 23. Let us now consider each case in the light of the above position of law. 

 25. AKM Abu Taher, petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3007 of 1998, would have vacated the office of director of the respondent No. 3 National Bank Ltd. on the expiry of two months from 24-8-1995, the date of service of notice on him under section 17(1) of the said Act. But the vacancy could not occur due to the order of stay in the ''earlier Writ Petition No. 2179 of 1995. It appears from respondent No. 1''s letter dated 6-1-96 (Annexure-C) and dated 13-2-96 (Annexure-D (I) that respondent No. 1 gave no objection to the rescheduling of the loan of Zita Garments for payment of which petitioner executed a guarantee bond. Though it was done during pendency of the earlier Rule the said Rule was discharged as the petitioner failed to show that he complied with the terms and conditions of such rescheduling. It is not the case of this petitioner that on full payment of the liabilities under the guarantee bond he was absolved of the said guarantee. So, there is no question of application of the provisions of sub-section (6) of section 17 of the said Act in his case. He having continued to function as director of respondent No. 3 in spite of discharge of the earlier Rule respondent No. 1 had no option but to bring the matter to the notice of the Chairman of Board of Directors of the respondent No. 3 by the impugned notice. On consideration of the materials on record and above position of law we find no illegality in the impugned notice dated 17-9-95 (Annexure-A) which was merely an intimation of the effect of notice under section 17(1) of the said Act after discharge of the Rule in Writ Petition No. 2179 of 1995. So we find no merit in this Rule. 

 26. Abdul Awal Mintoo, petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3008 of 1998, would have vacated the office of director of the respondent No. 3 National Bank Ltd on the expiry of two months from 9-9-95, the date of service of notice on him under section 17(1) of the said Act. But the vacancy could not occur due to the order of stay in the earlier Writ Petition No. 2298 of 1995 and Civil Miscellaneous petition. "It appears from respondent No. 1's letter dated 6-10-97 (Annexure-F) that the respondent No. 1 gave approval for release of the petitioner from the liability of the guarantee of Taka 10 lacs given by him for the loan of Niaz Mahmood Khan. Similarly, from respondent No. is letter dated 5-4-97 (Annexure-F I) it appears that respondent No. 1 gave approval on certain conditions for release of the petitioner from the liability of the guarantee given by him for the loan of SM Ashraful Islam. Similarly, it appears that respondent No. 1 gave approval for release of the petitioner from the liability of guarantee of Taka 6 lac given by him for the loan of Alamgir Sarker by its letter dated 30-10-97 (Annexure-F(3) that respondent No.1 gave approval for release of the petitioner from the liability of guarantee of Taka 8 lac given by him for the loan of Baharuddin Khelon. It may be mentioned here that in the earlier Writ Petition it was held that the petitioner had no liability for the loan of his brother Akbar Hossain. It further appears from another letter dated 10-8-97 (Annexure-E (I) sent by joint director of respondent No. 1 to the Managing Director of respondent No. 3 that if ov er due loan is paid by a director or rescheduled with the approval of the Board of Directors; of the concerned Bank and respondent No.1 then effectiveness of the said notice automatically ceases. Thus it appears that the petitioner was released from the aforesaid liabilities either during the pendency of the earlier Rule or Civil Miscellaneous Petition and operation of the order of stay in those cases and, as such, operation of his disqualification under sub-section (6) of section 17 of the said Act could not start till dismissal of Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 258 on 29-4-98 filed by him. He having continued to function as director of respondent No. 3 in spite of discharge of the earlier Rule and Civil Miscellaneous Petition respondent No. 1 had no option but to bring the matter to notice of the Chairman of Board of Directors of respondent No. 3 by the impugned notice. On consideration of the materials on record and above position of law we find no illegality in the impugned notice dated 17-9-98 (Annexure-A) which is merely an intimation of the effect of notice under section 17(I) of the said Act after discharge of the Rule in Writ Petition No. 2298 of 1995 and dismissal of Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 258/97 on 29-4-98. We also find no reason to treat letter dated 10-8-97 as withdrawal of the said notice under section 17(1) of the said Act as the petitioner failed to perform his obligations under the aforesaid bank guarantees within 2 months from the date of receipt of the said notice. So, we find no merit in this Rule also. 

 27. Abu Taher Miah, petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3109 of 1998, would have vacated the office of Director of respondent No. 3 National Bank Ltd on the expiry of two months from 25-9-95, the date of service of notice on him under section 17(1) of the said Act. But the vacancy could not occur due to the order of stay in the earlier Writ Petition and Civil Miscellaneous Petition. It appears from respondent No. Is letter dated 6-10-97 (Annexure-D) that respondent No. 1 gave its approval for release of the petitioner from the liability of the guarantee of Taka 2 lac given by him for the loan of Selina Trading Corporation. It was done during the pendency of Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 259 of 1997 filed by the petitioner and operation of the order of stay and, as such, his disqualification under sub-section (5) of section 17 of the said Act could not start till dismissal of Civil Miscellaneous Petition on 29-4-98. But he having continued to function as director of respondent No. 3 in spite of discharge of earlier Rule and dismissal of Civil Miscellaneous Petition respondent No. 1 had no option but to bring the matter to the notice of the Chairman of the Board of Directors of respondent Nos. 3 by the impugned notice. On consideration of the materials on record and above position of law we find no illegality in the impugned notice dated 17-9-98 (Annexure-A) which was as intimation of effect of notice under section 17(1) of the said Act after discharge of Rule in Writ Petition No. 2451 of 1995. So we find no merit in this Rule also. 

 28. Bazal Ahmed, petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3421 of 1998, would have vacated the office of director of respondent No.1, United Commercial Bank Ltd on the expiry of two months from 2-9-95, the date of service of notice on him under section 17(1) of the said Act. But the vacancy could not occur due to the order of stay in the earlier Writ Petition. It appears from respondent No. Is letter dated 15-4-97 (Annexure-G) that loan of the petitioner was rescheduled by the respondent No. 1 subject to certain conditions. It further appears from letter dated 15-9-97 (Annexure-J) that respondent No. 1 changed one of the conditions of rescheduling of the said loan. By latter dated 12-7-98 (Annexure-K) respondent No. 1 enhanced the limit of the loan of the petitioner. On the other hand, it appears from letter dated 13-8-98 (Annexure-Y-2) and Telex dated 9-3-99 (Annexure-Y-3) that the petitioner paid instalment up to May, 1998 and subsequent instalments could not be realised and the sum of Taka 97,74,857.00 as on 6-3-99 had fallen due on account of non-payment of instalments from June, 1998. Since the petitioner did not make full payment of rescheduled loan, even failed to pay instalment dues from June, 1998, no question of application of the provisions of sub-section (6) of section 17 of the said Act arises in his case. He having continued to function as director of respondent No.4 in spite of discharge of the earlier Rule respondent No.1 had no option but to bring the matter to the notice of the respondent No.3, Chairman of the respondent No.4 by the impugned notice. On consideration of the materials on record and above position of law we find no illegality in the impugned notice dated 17-9-98 (Annexure-A) which was merely an intimation of the effect of notice under section 17(1) of the said Act after discharge of the Rule in Writ Petition No. 222 of 1995. So we find no merit in this Rule also. 

 30. Habibur Rahman, petitioner of Writ Petition No.3388 of 1998 and Md Yakub Ali, petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3724 of 1998 would have vacated the office of director of respondent No. 4, Pubali Bank Ltd. on the expiry of two months from 29-8-98, the date of service of notices on them under section 17(I) of the said Act. But the vacancies could not occur due to the order of stay in the earlier writ petition and leave petitions. It appears from letter dated 25-1-98 (Annexure-E) that respondent No.1 gave no objection to the proposal of the respondent No. 4 for rescheduling of the loan of Mr. Habibur Rahman and Mr Md Yakub Ali on account of their Chandra Spinning Mills Ltd subject to 10% down payment. It also appears from letters dated 22-4-98 (Annexure-L) of Pubali Bank Ltd., that they paid 10% down payment as directed by the respondent No.1. It appears from letters dated 17-9-90 (Annexure-M) of the respondent No.1 that directorship of Mr. Habibur Rahman and Mr. Md Yakub Ali had fallen vacant on the expiry of 2 months from 29-8-98 and Rules in Writ Petition Nos. 2185 and 2186 of 1995 filed by them were also discharged. In reply to that letter Chairman of the Board-of Directors of respondent No. 4 by letter dated 2-9-98 (Annexure-Y) informed the respondent No.1 that in spite of discharge of the aforesaid Rules and subsequent rescheduling of the loan directorship of those two persons was continuing. Thereafter by impugned letters dated 29-9-98 (Annexure-O in both the Rules) respondent No.1. informed Chairman of the respondent No. 4 that after vacation of the office of directors under section 17(1) of the said Act by those persons from the date of full payment of the entire liability they shall remain ineligible to become director for one year under section 17(6) of the said Act. It is not the case of the petitioner of each of these two Rules that they paid the entire loan on account of the said spinning Mills. Rather their case is that they transferred their entire shares in the said Mills and resigned from the directorship of that Mills and the purchasers were elected directors in their place and they agreed to execute personal guarantees for the said loan in place of the petitioner of each of the two Rules. Thus it is clear that petitioner of each of the two Rules did not •pay the entire dues of the respondent No. 4. So, on consideration of the materials on record we find no illegality in the impugned letter dated 29-9-98 (Annexure-O). Hence we find no merit in these two Rules. 

 31. It may be ''mentioned that petitioner of each of the Rules in spite of discharge of the Rule in the Writ Petition earlier filed by them and dismissal of the Civil Miscellaneous petition filed by some of them continued to function as director of the respective Bank in spite of their office of director falling vacant. When the law came to the notice of Bangladesh Bank impugned letters were sent to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the respondent Bank. Except Chairman of Board of Directors of Pubali Bank Ltd, Chairman of the Board of Directors of other Banks did not protest to the letter dated 17-9-98 of the respondent No.1 in his letter dated 22-9-98 (Annexure-N) of Writ Petition Nos.3388 and 3724 of 1998) he stated that in spite of discharge of Rules in Writ Petition No.2185 and 2186 of 1995 due to rescheduling of the loan in question with the approval of respondent No. 1 there is no scope for the application of the provisions of section 17 of the said Act in respect of Habibur Rahman and Yakub Ali. Such contention was not acceptable to the respondent No.1. So impugned letters dated 29-9-98 (Annexure-O in both the Rules) were sent to him stating the latter legal position. In spite of the same petitioner of each of the Rules either challenged letter dated 17-9-98 or letter dated 29-9-98 in these Rules. 

 32. In the above facts and circumstances we find that petitioner of each of the Rules has been unnecessarily harassing the respondent No.1 by repeatedly filing cases and, as such, should be made liable to pay heavy cost to the respondent No.1. 

 In the result, all the Rules in Writ Petitions are discharged with cost of Taka 10,000.00 to be paid by the petitioner of each of Writ Petitions to the respondent No.1 Bangladesh Bank. Rule in contempt case No. 3 of 1999 is also discharged.
